function_question: How does nature keep its balance?

opening.text: There was a girl called Ivy who was the youngest engineer at the Idea Pop circus. She fixed the swings, the spotlights and the squeaky trapeze.
Ivy helped get ready for the biggest night of the year: the Season 2 finale show, starring a brave little toy acrobat on a tightrope.
At the last rehearsal, the acrobat wobbled and toppled off the string, again and again. "The show is tonight!" Ivy gasped. "How can I keep our star from falling?"

card.place: The Idea Pop circus show, the Season 2 finale
card.problem: The star toy acrobat keeps falling off the tightrope
card.goal: Make a toy that balances on a string and survives a wobble
card.rules: It must stay on for at least 10 seconds after a gentle tap

guide.brief: I'm Popi, your story guide, and welcome to the Season 2 grand finale! The circus star, a toy acrobat, keeps falling off the tightrope, and the show is tonight. Can you help Ivy keep it on the string? Let's start!
guide.your_idea: After a whole season of missions, you might already have a spark of an idea. Do you?
guide.nature_clues: Nature is full of balance champions. Tap each card to meet four heroes who stay steady on one leg, a thin fence or in mid-air!
guide.design_secret: Here's the secret all four heroes share…
guide.skill: Scientists predict before they test. Where should the clay go to keep the acrobat on the string the longest?
guide.sketch: Time to draw your acrobat and mark its balance point, like a real engineer!
guide.build_and_test: Build your acrobat, tap the string and start the clock. How long can your star stay on after a wobble?
guide.retry_tip: Engineers never stop at round 1, not even in the finale! Change ONE thing and test again!
guide.ending: And ever since then, the Idea Pop circus has a star acrobat that never falls, built like YOURS. What a way to finish Season 2! Take a bow, and get ready for the next adventure!

quick_check.question: Ivy's first acrobat stays on the string for 12 seconds after a tap. After she lowers the weight, it stays on for 48 seconds. How many times longer is that?
quick_check.right: Right! 48 ÷ 12 = 4. Lowering the weight made it last 4 times longer!
quick_check.wrong: Not quite. Divide the new time by the old time: 48 ÷ 12.

clue_cards.name: Cat
clue_cards.trick: It swings its tail the opposite way when it starts to tip.
clue_cards.does: The tail swing pulls it back into balance, and helps it twist to land on its feet.

clue_cards.name: Gecko
clue_cards.trick: It swings its tail in mid-air during a leap.
clue_cards.does: The tail turns its body back the right way so it lands safely.

clue_cards.name: Flamingo
clue_cards.trick: Its body weight sits right above its foot and its joints lock.
clue_cards.does: It stands on one leg for hours with almost no effort.

clue_cards.name: Tightrope walker
clue_cards.trick: They carry a long pole that droops down at both ends.
clue_cards.does: The pole puts weight low and wide, so wobbles are slow and easy to fix.

match_groups.label: 🔁 Swings a tail to fix a wobble

predict.prompt: Tips over or swings back? Predict first!

items.label: A pencil balanced on its point
A balancing-bird toy with heavy wing tips below its beak

predict.explain: When the balance point is above the support, a wobble makes things tip over. When the balance point is below the support, gravity pulls it back to the middle, so it swings back instead of falling.

lab.title: The wobble lab
lab.predict: Put a small ball of clay on your card acrobat. Where will it help the acrobat stay on the string the longest after a tap?
options: Clay hanging below on bent arms
lab.measure: seconds it stays on after a tap

tool.name: Nature Translator
tool.intro: The Nature Translator turns a design problem into a question for nature, then turns nature's answer back into a trick you can build. For the finale, you'll use all 4 steps, from start to finish, like a real biomimicry designer!

parts.name: Function
parts.example: 🪖 It must protect a head in a crash.

parts.name: Nature question
parts.what: Turn the function into "How does nature…?"
parts.example: 🪖 How does nature protect against impact?

parts.name: Strategy
parts.what: Which living thing does it, and how?
parts.example: 🪖 A woodpecker's spongy skull bone soaks up the shock.

parts.name: Design principle
parts.what: Say the trick in plain words, without the animal.
parts.example: 🪖 A spongy layer that squashes slowly makes a softer stop.

sketch_checklist: I drew my acrobat on the tightrope from the front.
I marked the support point and the centre of mass.
I showed where I added weight and how low it hangs.

test.measure: seconds it stays on the string after a wobble
test.check_question: Wobble check: what happened after the tap?

reflection.question: Which balance trick was the star of your act?
